title: Value: NPV by start year, risk reduction from PoF/RUL, weighted value

questions.heading: NPV by Start Year Is One Cash Flow, Shifted and Discounted to One Date
questions.stem: Two analysts value a project's 2031 start. One discounts every amount to 2027, the plan's first year; the other discounts every amount to 2031, the start year. Whose table charges the project for waiting?

options.text: The one discounting to 2027, since each year of delay costs a year of discounting
options.says: Right: the lesson discounts every start to 2027, and says valuing each start from its own year makes waiting look free.

options.text: The one discounting to 2031, since each start is valued on the date its money moves
options.says: Valuing each start from its own year "would make waiting look free".

options.text: Both of them, since a change of valuation date only rescales the whole table
options.says: Discounting to each start's own year changes each start by a different factor, so it is not a rescaling of the table.

options.text: Neither of them, since waiting is charged only through the benefit's decay
options.says: In P086's table each year of delay costs a year of discounting on benefit and costs, plus the decay.

questions.heading: Risk Reduction Starts From the RUL, Made a Point on the Weibull Curve
questions.stem: An asset's catalog scale is 40 years. Its predicted RUL becomes the median remaining life only with a scale of 45, the shape kept. Compared with the catalog curve, what does the anchored curve do to the risk a replacement removes?

options.text: It raises it at every start, since a longer life gives the work more value to keep
options.says: A larger scale means fewer expected failures each year, so less risk to remove: A086's anchored scale 41.3 against 37.8 removed less at every start.

options.text: It leaves it unchanged, since the RUL moves the median but the shape decides the risk
options.says: The yearly risk uses the scale too; A086's coefficients changed from 124.7 to 97.2 in 2027.

options.text: It raises it for late starts and lowers it for early ones, since the asset ages meanwhile
options.says: A086's anchored coefficient was lower at all four starts.

options.text: It lowers it at every start, since the asset's expected failures are lower each year
options.says: Right: as with A086, a larger scale means fewer expected failures, and the replacement removes about a fifth less.

questions.heading: Weighted Value Divides by Fixed References and Weights by Swing Ratings
questions.stem: A colleague changes the NPV reference from $5,000k to $5,001k to see what happens, and the plan the model chooses does not move. What does the milestone's test suite report?

options.text: Nothing, since the plan the model chooses is still the same plan
options.says: The tables are pinned by digest: "any change to a formula, a reference or a weight is a failed test".

options.text: A failed test on the value table's digest, though no plan changed
options.says: Right: every value moves slightly, so the pinned value digest changes; the NPV and risk tables do not use the reference.

options.text: A failed test on the NPV table's digest, since the reference is an amount of NPV
options.says: The NPV table is the cash-flow formula with no reference in it; only the value table divides by references.

options.text: Failed tests on all three digests, since the three tables are pinned as one record
options.says: Each table has its own digest; only the value table depends on the reference.
